reason: Telipinu is the Hittite god of grain and vegetation; the Telipinu Myth (CTH 324) explains agricultural fertility as his active presence and famine as his absence.
When Telipinu vanishes, springs dry up and the land thirsts; his return restores freshwater and irrigation to the Anatolian plain.
The myth is a ritual negotiation with divine anger and withdrawal — a Hittite model of restoring relationship, balance, and communal wellbeing after rupture.
